precepts.text: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it.
precepts.point: A captain charged after an attack on him and his wife was cleared when video showed he defended himself. Many had already believed the one-sided account.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.” If you lie on somebody and run with slander, it says that you hate the one who is afflicted by it.

You heard it plainly from one of them: I am here to down IUIC. That is the hatred behind the lying tongue that Psalms 101 says God will cut off.

Every matter is to be established by two or three witnesses. What was put out about Captain Obadiah was one witness, and that witness was a lie. The charges were dropped; the footage and the witnesses showed he was defending himself. It is sad that the white man had to come and say he was defending himself, when those who talk about righteous judgment could not understand something that simple. In London, when our sister died, people said IUIC killed her and hid evidence, and the investigators showed that the man who did it was evil and we had nothing to do with it.

A false witness is called slander, or defamation, and false witness can get you killed. By the law, what was to be done to the brother you slandered is to be done unto you. We do not have power to institute that, but Esau’s court system has defamation, and that is how it is going to be done now: whatever you put out against the truth, you had better be able to prove it, or you will have to come up out of the pockets. That is to protect the ministry of Christ, because the lies are put out to blame the ministry.

precepts.text: Where no talebearer is, the strife ceaseth; messy people feed the fire.
precepts.point: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: much strife and contention comes from messy people. Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
“Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.” Much strife and contention comes from messy people; they are the wood that keeps the fire going.

Repent of that messy spirit; it has no place in Israel. Take away the talebearer and the strife ceases.

precepts.text: Correction and work are appointed for a servant, matching the rod for the fool's back.
precepts.point: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.” Each one has what is fitted to it, and what fits the fool is the rod.

Ecclesiasticus says the same: “Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant.” Correction and work are appointed for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. The ass gets the wand and the burdens; the servant gets bread, correction and work.

That is why honor is not seemly for a fool, like snow in summer and rain in harvest. What is fitted to him is not honor but the rod.

precepts.text: Those who escape the world through knowing Christ and turn back are worse than before; it is the true proverb of the dog returning to his vomit and the washed sow to the mire.
precepts.point: As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.” Peter quotes this and calls it a true proverb, which shows the apostles quoted Solomon.

“For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning.” Those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. “For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them.”

Then Peter brings Solomon: “But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire.” The fool going back to his folly is the man who knew the way of righteousness and turned from the holy commandment: the dog back at his vomit and the washed sow back in the mire.

precepts.text: Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you.
precepts.point: As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?"

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.” Grab a dog by the ears and you are going to get bitten; that is what meddling in strife that is not yours gets you.

Ecclesiasticus gives the same warning: “Strive not in a matter that concerneth thee not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.” Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you.

A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage. She took the dog by the ears in strife that was not hers. The Bible is a true book.

precepts.text: Nothing is covered that shall not be revealed, nor hid that shall not be known.
precepts.point: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High.

note.label: Proverbs 26: Honor Is Not Fitting for a Fool

precepts.why:
“Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” The man who hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him; there are seven abominations in his heart. But his cover does not hold: his wickedness is put out on display before the whole congregation.

Christ says why: “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.” Hatred covered by deceit is still covered, and nothing covered stays covered. It will be revealed and known.

Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit. That thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High.
